audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for gate assembly, unnamed nearer redeemer, Naomi's land transaction, redemption disclosure, Ruth/Mahlon name-continuity clause, inheritance concern, sandal custom, witness formulas, Rachel/Leah/Tamar blessing, conception language, women's blessing of Naomi, goel child language, better-than-seven-sons praise, Naomi's caregiving role, neighborhood naming, Obed/Jesse/David link, and Perez genealogy.

verses.restored: Boaz went up to gate and sat there. Look, the redeemer of whom Boaz had spoken was passing by. He said, Turn aside, sit here, so-and-so. He turned aside and sat.

familiar.text: Then went Boaz up to the gate, and sat him down there: and, behold, the kinsman of whom Boaz spake came by; unto whom he said, Ho, such a one! turn aside, sit down here. And he turned aside, and sat down.

modern.text: Meanwhile, Boaz went to the gate and sat down there. Soon the kinsman-redeemer of whom he had spoken came along, and Boaz said, “Come over here, my friend, and sit down.” So he went over and sat down.

original.text: וּבֹ֨עַז עָלָ֣ה הַשַּׁעַר֮ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שָׁם֒ וְהִנֵּ֨ה הַגֹּאֵ֤ל עֹבֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר בֹּ֔עַז וַיֹּ֛אמֶר ס֥וּרָה שְׁבָה פֹּ֖ה פְּלֹנִ֣י אַלְמֹנִ֑י וַיָּ֖סַר וַיֵּשֵֽׁב

modern.text: Then Boaz took ten of the elders of the city and said, “Sit here,” and they did so.

modern.text: And he said to the kinsman-redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the land of Moab, is selling the piece of land that belonged to our brother Elimelech.

verses.restored: I said, I will uncover your ear, saying, Acquire it before those sitting here and before elders of my people. If you will redeem, redeem. If you will not redeem, tell me, so I may know, because there is no one besides you to redeem, and I am after you. He said, I will redeem.

familiar.text: And I thought to advertise thee, saying, Buy it before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people. If thou wilt redeem it, redeem it: but if thou wilt not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know: for there is none to redeem it beside thee; and I am after thee. And he said, I will redeem it.

modern.text: I thought I should inform you that you may buy it back in the presence of those seated here and in the presence of the elders of my people. If you want to redeem it, do so. But if you will not redeem it, tell me so I may know, because there is no one but you to redeem it, and I am next after you.” “I will redeem it,” he replied.

verses.restored: Boaz said, On day you acquire field from hand of Naomi, you also acquire Ruth the Moabite, wife of the dead, to raise name of dead upon his inheritance.

familiar.text: Then said Boaz, What day thou buyest the field of the hand of Naomi, thou must buy it also of Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance.

modern.text: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the land from Naomi and also from Ruth the Moabitess, you must also acquire the widow of the deceased in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance.”

familiar.text: And the kinsman said, I cannot redeem it for myself, lest I mar mine own inheritance: redeem thou my right to thyself; for I cannot redeem it.

modern.text: The kinsman-redeemer replied, “I cannot redeem it myself, or I would jeopardize my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption, because I cannot redeem it.”

verses.restored: Now this was formerly in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to establish every matter: a man removed his sandal and gave it to his neighbor. This was the testimony in Israel.

familiar.text: Now this was the manner in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things; a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour: and this was a testimony in Israel.

modern.text: Now in former times in Israel, concerning the redemption or exchange of property, to make any matter legally binding a man would remove his sandal and give it to the other party, and this was a confirmation in Israel.

translation_notes: The gate proceeding is public economic law involving land, kinship, inheritance, and household continuity. Public witness offers accountability, but women remain discussed within male-governed structures.
The nearer redeemer is left unnamed—'so-and-so' or an intentionally concealed name. His refusal concerns his inheritance; the text does not require inventing moral defects beyond what is stated.

Verses 5 and 10 use acquisition language for land and for Ruth's marriage within an ancient patriarchal legal system. Reporting that language must not make Ruth property or erase the necessity of consent.
Ruth remains 'the Moabite' even as she enters a Bethlehem household and genealogy. Belonging does not require ethnic erasure, xenophobia, or contempt for Moabites.
The duty to raise the dead man's name combines family continuity with property transmission. It is related to, but not a simple enactment of, the levirate law in Deuteronomy 25.
The sandal exchange is described as an older legal custom and public testimony. It is not humiliation of the unnamed redeemer and should not be reconstructed beyond the text.

The blessing invokes Rachel, Leah, and Tamar—women whose stories include reproductive struggle, exploitation, rivalry, and constrained agency. Their names must not become decorative validation of patriarchy.

YHWH gives conception in the narrative, but fertility is not proof of virtue, Divine favor, womanhood, or successful marriage. Infertility, pregnancy loss, childlessness, and nonparenthood are not spiritual failures.

The women call the child a redeemer for Naomi and praise Ruth as better than seven sons. This honors a foreign daughter-in-law above a conventional ideal of male offspring; it does not reduce Ruth to reproduction.
Naomi becomes the child's caregiver or foster-mother. Her restored community and purpose matter, but a baby does not erase bereavement or make older women valuable only through caregiving.
'A son has been born to Naomi' is communal kinship language, not denial that Ruth is the child's mother.

The genealogy connects the story to David. It must not erase Ruth and Naomi beneath a royal endpoint, authorize monarchy uncritically, or support Christian supersessionism over Jewish scripture and identity.
safety_note: Do not treat Ruth as purchased property, marriage as automatic consent, childbirth as women's purpose, or fertility as moral reward. Preserve Ruth's Moabite identity, Naomi's grief and caregiving dignity, public accountability, and the difference between ancient kinship law and modern ethical relationships.
